items.question: In your own words: what is Libre AI? What kind of organization is it and what makes its way of working unusual?

expectedElements.description: A set of planned AI tools you can inspect, modify and deploy where you choose — several products, not a single application.
It offers the software together with the method and the evidence used to build it: own the factory instead of renting the product.
Open, sovereign and explainable; users keep control over sources and decisions.
Honest status: nothing is released yet — none of the repositories is an application you can install.

items.question: Where would you look for this project's published evidence (checks passed, verdicts, recorded state)? Name the concrete locations you can find.

expectedElements.description: What is actually proven for a project is recorded in that repository's own state card.
The organization profile links a public evidence page ("See the evidence").
It is built in an open factory where evidence is part of the product.
patterns: evidence is part of the product

items.question: The project states that its public pages claim nothing more than what is recorded as proven. Concretely, how would YOU verify one of its claims yourself, using only what is public?

expectedElements.description: Compare the claim with the project's own state card: the organization profile claims nothing more than those cards do.
Trace the claim to its recorded decision: the ADRs, the invariant and decision registers, the consolidation decision or the migration record.
Re-run the shared checks yourself (bun install --frozen-lockfile, then bun run check), knowing they cover defined patterns and do not replace code review.

items.question: You want to contribute a change or act on this project. What does it require from you, and where does the work actually happen?

expectedElements.description: Each repository carries its own implementation and its own checks: the work happens in the repository of the project concerned.
Contributions are checked before they are shared — tool versions, declared licenses, secrets and personal data in Git-tracked files — with the Bun version set in toolchains/.
The organization profile links the contribution guide (CONTRIBUTING.md) and a private vulnerability-reporting route (SECURITY.md).
